title: Funeral home crematorium approved despite tenant displacement concerns
subtitle: Sportsworld and Courtland developments, Biehn Drive studies, Municipal Housing Pledge, e-bike subsidies, dangerous dog appeal, neighbourhood associations.
overview: Council approved the Official Plan and zoning changes for a funeral home expansion and crematorium at 507 Frederick Street and 40 and 44 Becker Street {{vote:m3}}. The version approved leaves out 48 Becker Street, so those rental homes stay. Debate centred on the loss of low-cost rental housing against the needs of a growing local business.

Council also approved two housing developments: 45-53 Courtland Avenue East {{vote:m2}} and a high-intensity mixed-use project at Sportsworld, King Street East {{vote:m4}}. On the Biehn Drive sewer and road extension, Council sent the environmental study back for more work, with a report due in late 2023 or early 2024 {{vote:m5}}.

Council adopted Kitchener's Municipal Housing Pledge to the province, including the target of 35,000 new homes by 2031 {{vote:m23}}. It asked the federal government to subsidize e-bikes and e-scooters {{vote:m16}}. It also directed staff to report on better use of community centres {{vote:m21}} and confirmed a dangerous dog designation with a flexible deadline for sterilization {{vote:m1}}.
The Mayor also reported that the Region's managed encampment site will open for move-in on April 15.

decisions.item: Funeral home expansion and crematorium, 507 Frederick Street
decisions.detail: Council adopted the Official Plan and zoning changes and approved a crematorium, excluding 48 Becker Street from the application {{vote:m3}}.
Council adopted the Official Plan amendment and approved the zoning change for the Cantiro Courtland project {{vote:m2}}.
Council approved the land-use change to Mixed Use, the zoning change, and the Urban Design Brief for 4396 King Street East and 25 Sportsworld Drive {{vote:m4}}.

decisions.item: Biehn Drive and sanitary trunk sewer extension
decisions.detail: Council directed staff to do more studies and one more consultation, using the remaining 2020 budget, and report back in late 2023 or early 2024 {{vote:m5}}.
Council approved submitting the Municipal Housing Pledge to the province {{vote:m23}}.
Council confirmed the committee's decision to affirm the designation, amended so the sterilization deadline can follow veterinarian advice {{vote:m1}}.
Council asked the federal government to subsidize e-bikes and e-scooters, especially for low-income residents, and to send the resolution to the Premier and others {{vote:m16}}.
Council approved the 2023 affiliation list and directed staff to report before summer recess on options for community centre partnerships, use and programming {{vote:m21}}.

debate: On the funeral home, delegates opposing the application raised the loss of affordable rental homes, displacement of tenants, traffic, air emissions and the added parking, citing the city's Housing for All and TransformWR commitments. Some councillors said they could not separate the human impact from the planning merits.

Supporters said the business is a small, locally owned operation whose services have grown, that cremation demand is rising, and that the applicant had already removed one property and offered tenants alternative units and relocation money. Several councillors noted a refusal could be appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal, where the original proposal could return.

On Sportsworld, staff said King Street already has peak-hour congestion that would not be significantly worsened by the project. New highway ramps are planned but not funded, and further traffic studies will be needed for each future application. The applicant's planner said geothermal systems are not allowed on the site.

On the housing pledge, one councillor asked whether Council was being pushed into a promise it cannot fully control. Staff replied that it reflects work already under way, that the 35,000-home figure was set by the province, and that Council controls approvals rather than construction.
On Biehn Drive, delegates paused their presentations and supported more study of the wetland. Staff said the traffic study will be updated with and without the road extension.
